\begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch3:3-25↗ prob:diffeomorphism-pseudohyperbolic-pseudosphere Let $(K^r(R), \bar{g}_R^2)$ be the $r$-dimensional ball of radius $R$ with the Beltrami--Klein metric (3.9), and let $\bar{\mathbb {H}}^{r,1}(R)$ be the product manifold $K^r(R) \times \mathbb {R}$ with the pseudo-Riemannian warped product metric $q = \bar{g}_R^2 \oplus (-f^2 dt^2)$, where $f: K^r(R) \to \mathbb {R}^+$ is given by \[ f(w) = \frac{R^2}{\sqrt{R^2 - |w|^2}}. \]

Define $F: \bar{\mathbb {H}}^{r,1}(R) \to \mathbb {R}^{r,2}$ by \[ F(w,t) = \frac{(Rw, R^2 \cos t, R^2 \sin t)}{\sqrt{R^2 - |w|^2}}. \]

Prove that the image of $F$ is the anti-de Sitter space $\mathbb {H}^{r,1}(R)$, and $F$ defines a pseudo-Riemannian covering of $(\mathbb {H}^{r,1}(R), q_R^{(r,1)})$ by $(\bar{\mathbb {H}}^{r,1}(R), q)$. [Remark: We are tacitly extending the notions of warped product metric and Riemannian coverings to the pseudo-Riemannian case in the obvious ways. It follows from the result of Problem 3-24 that $\mathbb {H}^{r,s}(R)$ is simply connected when $s \geq 2$ but $\mathbb {H}^{r,1}(R)$ is not. This shows that $(\bar{\mathbb {H}}^{r,1}(R), q)$, called universal anti-de Sitter space of radius $R$, is the universal pseudo-Riemannian covering manifold of $(\mathbb {H}^{r,1}(R), q_R^{(r,1)})$.] \end{exercise}
